answer: Use a ZK passport nullifier registry. 1) An NFC phone reads the passport chip and verifies its signature. 2) A circuit derives one nullifier from the document secret, hiding the traveler's name and number. 3) The contract accepts each nullifier once; epoch proofs rotate keys without breaking uniqueness. 4) Delegations branch like a vine, but never mint roots; members remain a nebula of unlinkable credentials. At $80 per procured identity, 1,000 sybils cost $80,000, a $90 NFC phone, and 333 hours at 20 minutes each. Like an ember that lights one hearth, each passport authorizes one root.
